derivation: A∩B uses x≥0, x≥n/6, and y≥0; squaring B is valid because A gives y>0.
The two curve equations become the symmetric system x^2+n=6y and y^2+n=6x.
Subtracting gives (x−y)(x+y+6)=0; nonnegative x,y make x+y+6 positive, so x=y.
On the diagonal, x^2−6x+n=0; exactly one diagonal solution requires the repeated-root condition 36−4n=0.
Therefore n=9, and the sole intersection is (3,3).
